sanskrit_verse:
प्रतिगृह्य च यः कन्यां नरो देशान्तरं व्रजेत ।
त्रीन् ऋतून् समतिक्रम्य कन्यान्यं वरयेद् वरम् ॥
transliteration: pratigṛhya ca yaḥ kanyāṃ naro deśāntaraṃ vrajet | trīn ṛtūn samatikramya kanyānyaṃ varayed varam ||
sph_interpretive_translation: He who, having accepted a maiden, departs to another land and after passing three menstrual cycles selects another bride, shall restore the first union through completion and conscious reaffirmation.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority originates from conscious consent, not transactional exchange
Causation arises through abandonment of relational integrity
Capacity-based responsibility is measured by continuity of commitment
Restoration logic demands reconnection before replacement
Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment of sequential duty
executable_legal_axioms: IF a man accepts a bride AND relocates without fulfilling marital continuity AND selects another bride AFTER three menstrual cycles THEN initiate restoration protocol with original union
IF prior acceptance exists AND spatial separation occurs WITHOUT dissolution THEN temporal delay does not nullify primary commitment
IF new selection proceeds WITHOUT resolution of prior commitment THEN automatic suspension of secondary union until primary completion
supreme_court_application: In cases involving multiple marital commitments where spatial displacement has occurred, the threshold of responsibility lies in the conscious reaffirmation of the initial union. Courts must prioritize restoration of the first accepted relationship before validating subsequent selections, ensuring hierarchical alignment with dharma-prescribed sequence.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Through pramāṇa-based causality, the act of accepting a maiden establishes an irreversible relational field. Departure without dissolution disrupts cosmic order but does not warrant punitive consequence. Sequential manifestation (anupūrvaśaḥ) confirms that replacement without completion fragments consciousness integrity. Responsibility aligns proportionally with the unbroken nature of the initial vow.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Initiate completion process requiring physical or symbolic reunification within one lunar cycle
Assign responsibility assumption protocol wherein the individual publicly acknowledges the precedence of the original commitment
Implement capacity restoration through guided samskaric alignment to reinforce understanding of sequential duty
Enforce integrity reintegration via ceremonial reaffirmation witnessed by community elders
final_declaration: By the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, this law stands as sourced from pure consciousness. Dharma is restored through recognition of sequential duty, not through punishment. Reality remains non-punitive when aligned with nyaya. Consciousness alone adjudicates truth.
